Revised assessment: The statement pairs upbeat real-side data (“solid” growth, low and stable unemployment) with a cautious stance on inflation (“somewhat elevated”), keeps the policy rate unchanged at a restrictive 4.25–4.50% range, and continues quantitative tightening via capped Treasury and MBS runoffs. In the New Keynesian/monetary-policy rule literature (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), holding a restrictive stance while inflation is above target is consistent with stabilization objectives and is not dovish. The state-contingent, data-dependent language aligns with Woodford’s forward-guidance principles, anchoring expectations without pre-committing to easing. Term-structure evidence (e.g., Cochrane–Piazzesi) implies ongoing balance-sheet runoff and a firm floor system (ON RRP/repo corridor) keep mild upward pressure on term premia, reinforcing a slightly hawkish tilt. An inflation-at-risk lens (Adrian et al.; and the referenced “Mixing it up: Inflation at risk”) supports vigilance against right-tail inflation outcomes, justifying balanced-risks language. Net tone: modestly positive on growth, neutral-to-slightly hawkish on policy.

Adjusted sentiment: 0.15 (lower than 0.25 to reflect the literature-consistent hawkish bias from continued QT and state-contingent guidance despite strong activity).
